agent_review.author: agent

findings.summary: The new behavior bundle whiteouted after 29 verified actions.
findings.observed_fact: Bushtank was the last survivor and fainted before Bite executed against Sunflora at 22 HP.
findings.strategic_judgment: This was a deterministic policy/preparation-line failure, not an emulator mismatch or an acceptable variance branch.
findings.next_test: Replay the corrected bundle from the identical precontact checkpoint and require a terminal win.
findings.state_unavailable_reason: The terminal state cannot replay the earlier causal decisions; separate turn-1, turn-15, and turn-22 states cover those causes.

findings.summary: An unproven generic Fake Out strategy overrode the proven Gavi opening on turn 1.

resolution.observed: Corrected policy selected Spark; Spark executed with the expected PP decrement and verified Super Fang reply.

findings.observed_fact: The engine chose Fake Out then Spark; Bibarel survived at 4 HP and forced a Lildozer pivot, while three prior clean identical-checkpoint wins opened Spark then Spark.
findings.strategic_judgment: Candidate strategies are suggestions, not safe unattended rules; auto-executing one changed the whole matchup sequence.
findings.next_test: From turn 1, require the corrected policy to select and execute Spark without applying fresh-entry-fake-out-tempo.

findings.summary: Bushtank abandoned its Eelektrik sacrifice line after one Razor Leaf on turn 15.

resolution.observed: Corrected policy selected Razor Leaf; it executed, damaged Eelektrik, and kept Bushtank in the sacrifice line.

findings.observed_fact: Switching Bushtank at 26 HP exposed Ohmnomnom and then Bugatti; prior clean runs kept using Razor Leaf until Bushtank fainted and gave Ohmnomnom a safe forced entry.
findings.strategic_judgment: The executable strategy encoded only the first Razor Leaf even though its declared line requires repeating the safest damage action.
findings.next_test: From turn 15, require Razor Leaf to remain selected and execute instead of a voluntary switch.

findings.summary: The Gavi profile forced 5-HP Bugatti to attempt Rollout into Dustox instead of taking the safe Birdlaw switch.

resolution.observed: Below the 18-HP threshold, the exception deactivated; Birdlaw switched in, survived Venoshock, and applied Intimidate.

findings.observed_fact: The certificate ranked Birdlaw as surviving, but the profile vetoed that switch; Bugatti fainted before Rollout executed.
findings.strategic_judgment: The matchup exception lacked the verified 18-HP survival threshold and therefore overrode survival with an impossible attack.
findings.next_test: From turn 22, require the low-HP exception to deactivate and Birdlaw to switch in successfully.

findings.summary: Croakatoa, Ohmnomnom, Bugatti, Birdlaw, and Bushtank were all consumed after the altered opening sequence.
findings.observed_fact: Every faint was RAM-verified; Croakatoa and Birdlaw dealt useful damage, but the roster reached Sunflora with no healthy answer.
findings.strategic_judgment: These are downstream effects of the three high-severity policy defects, not five independent trainer exceptions.
findings.next_test: Confirm the corrected opening and Eelektrik line preserve enough reserves to finish Sunflora and Dustox.

findings.summary: Eight switches occurred, but only the Bushtank-to-Ohmnomnom pivot was independently harmful.
findings.observed_fact: Five switches were forced replacements and the other two voluntary matchup entries acted productively; no consecutive no-action switch loop occurred.
findings.strategic_judgment: The review should fix the bad pivot without adding a blanket anti-switch rule that would break safe replacements.
findings.next_test: Audit the next clone for zero harmful voluntary pivots while preserving forced and matchup switches.

correct_choices: All 29 actions and enemy replies were verified with no tooling discrepancy.
Fake Out legality and fresh-entry reconstruction were correct even though the turn-1 strategic preference was not.
Lildozer safely finished Bibarel after the altered opening, and Birdlaw correctly used Aerial Ace to remove Dustox.
agent_review.next_test: Run bounded turn-1, turn-15, and turn-22 regressions; resolve their attached findings only after the corrected decisions execute, then restart qualification at Clone 1.
